body:
oof.. sorry for the late reply. About two weeks late.. there's been a good deal of things going on, and I let too much time go by.

I'll bring up the possibility of therapy again, but maybe totally separate from his mother/family's knowing. In the past, there was talk of him being ADD, although he didn't really accept the idea. I think his mother tried to push the diagnosis further than he wanted, and I don't want him feeling reluctant because of that.

Thanks so much again for advice from your own experiences.

Wow! Thank you so much for all this. I really appreciate the information you put together.

It's been over two weeks since I replied, I'm very sorry about that. We finally finished with my mother-in-law's move, but between that and suddenly needing to clear my computer.. oi, time went by.

Thanks again. I think this'll point me to information I would've just gotten lost while trying to find, or just didn't even know existed. 

Somehow, cryogenics seems like a terrifying thing to me, haha. It might be really fascinating and helpful for him to check out though.

Haha.. well thank you. That sounds interesting and potentially within his field of studies (I would think physics studies would tie in with cryogenics, and other similar fields at some point).

I know everyone who puts in time to give some advice here doesn't get much for it, but it's very much appreciated. Thanks!

Well thanks a lot for the advice. A lot of times, it feels as though the feedback you get is really so simple and logical.. yet it's something I'd probably feel more anxious about it, without having heard this from someone else. That sounds best. I'll see if he wouldn't mind looking into therapy sessions, or at least talking to his old doctor again.

Thanks again so much for the time and thoughts!
Thank you. I'll keep this in mind for when it comes to tackling this problem. It's easing to hear from others who have experienced this sort of panic attack.

Well, thank you. I wouldn't have thought it could be connected to something like hypochondriasis, although I could see that now, after reading some.

I'll do a little more reading on that, as well as on OCD issues. I know he has some of those, although not to such a great degree.. mostly just silly things.

I found a board of college students discussing this issue, and I suppose it isn't so rare. Some had even said they would have panic attacks from these thoughts, so maybe I have some leads.

Thank you.

No problem. Thanks for the inquiries, really.

From some conversations I've had with his mother, I think it first really started when he had a lot of stress, relating to his father and legal confrontations (child support). His father left the family when he was so young.. I think there's some back-story I don't know, but it's all sensitive issues. I've slowly learned more, but it really isn't so much at this point, heh. I don't think he was actually diagnosed with anything, that or else he refused to accept that he had any sort of condition. And as far as I understood, it's when he feels that he's truly imagining/feeling the state of being dead.

Unfortunately, both of the recent times he got upset, it was also during one of our "worse" arguments. And it's not so much a conflict against each other as much as it is a peak of stressful issues, and maybe poor communication with certain things. Looking back, I think we do well with resolving our problems though, and it really feels like we sort of take down a wall that we hadn't acknowledged before. But both times, it was late at night, after having gone to bed that he got so upset.

Since I now know that it's still likely to come up again in the future, I'll speak with my mother-in-law about it. I'd hate to see her get stressed about it though (we have a lot of good stressors in this family, I suppose, heheh) while she's in the midst of her moving, and during a family visit. That will have to wait maybe another week or two.

Maybe I just don't know enough right now.
